budget_items.what_was_said: The Town Manager said the Governor's first cherry sheet had been released, raising the state aid figure and total revenue slightly from the prior update.

budget_items.topic: available levy revenue after non-appropriated expenses
budget_items.what_was_said: After subtracting non-appropriated expenses, state assessments, and last year's capital-plan levy set-aside, this is what remains available for appropriation.
Comparing available revenue to FY26 appropriations (excluding the extra $500,000 given to schools) yields the new money available for FY27.

budget_items.topic: potential revenue split among school, town, Monty Tech
budget_items.what_was_said: A hypothetical distribution of the new FY27 revenue based on each entity's share of the budget was presented, with school at 53.3%, town at 43.91%, and Monty Tech at 2.76%.
The Town Manager noted Monty Tech sets its own assessment rather than accepting a proportional split; last year's increase was used as an example that exceeds the proportional share.
The health insurance trust's initial 20% warning came down after GLP-1 drugs were dropped from coverage; the average and high increases were given, with the town's own number due in mid-February.

budget_items.topic: health insurance impact on school and town budgets
budget_items.what_was_said: Applying the higher health-insurance estimate to a traditional budget split leaves little of the new revenue remaining for schools or town after paying for the increase.

budget_items.topic: total health insurance increase (school, town, retirees)
budget_items.what_was_said: Combined across school, town and retirees, the health insurance increase was described as non-negotiable barring plan design changes.
A described 10% increase in the county retirement assessment was called non-negotiable.
School transportation costs were cited as another fixed cost driver for FY27.
Adding a fourth shift to the fire department's operating budget, not including associated health insurance, was quantified as a major cost driver.

budget_items.topic: running deficit after major cost drivers
budget_items.what_was_said: Starting from new FY27 revenue and subtracting health insurance, retirement, transportation and the fourth fire shift in sequence, the Town Manager walked the board down to a negative balance.

The Town Manager said the deficit shown covers only four items and does not include utilities, vendor contracts, TCP carrying costs, pavement management restoration, the actual Monty Tech assessment, or collective bargaining increases, putting the full deficit higher.
A school committee member stated the total level-service school budget figure and how much it is over FY26, including the 20% health insurance assumption.
A board member noted school-choice revenue on the cherry sheet has fallen sharply from what it used to bring in, shifting that cost onto taxpayers.
A board member argued the recycling program's cost has grown substantially since the start of COVID with no action taken to address it.
The Town Manager again floated eliminating the mosquito control assessment as a savings option, noting past public pushback.

budget_items.topic: health insurance and transportation cost drivers (school side)
budget_items.what_was_said: A school committee member said health insurance adds a large amount per employee beyond salary, and that transportation costs rose substantially with no reimbursement since Lunenburg is not a regional district.

decisions.decision: The tri-board agreed it needs to settle on an override number in time to be placed on the ballot by the town's April 10th deadline.
The school committee agreed to supply updated staffing data including last year's layoffs, which were missing from the FY16-FY25 headcount chart presented.
The tri-board set its next joint meeting for February 9th, to be held at the middle-high school.
The school committee agreed to hold a separate session addressing the outstanding FY25 questions (the prior override whose funds had to be returned) before the wider public forum.
The Town Manager agreed to send the board members the state's Prop 2½ override-options guidance and the campaign-finance rules for elected officials discussing an override.

minutes.headline: Town, school and finance officials agree Lunenburg likely needs a property-tax override to close a large FY27 budget gap
minutes.summary: This joint "tri-board" meeting of the Select Board, School Committee and Finance Committee opened with extensive public comment from firefighters and school staff describing understaffing and burnout, followed by a Town Manager presentation showing updated state aid and revenue figures leaving a large projected FY27 deficit once health insurance, retirement, transportation and a fourth fire shift are covered. The boards debated how to communicate the gap without "scare tactics," discussed override structures and cost-saving options (recycling, school choice, mosquito control), sparred over whether school staffing has actually been cut, and set a February 9th follow-up meeting without settling on an override amount.

what_happened.line: Town, school and finance officials agreed Lunenburg likely needs a property-tax override to close a projected FY27 gap, without settling on an amount or structure
The Town Manager walked the boards from updated state aid down through health insurance, retirement, transportation and a fourth fire shift to a remaining deficit
Finance and school committee members disputed whether district staffing has actually been cut, and the school committee agreed to supply updated data including last year's layoffs
The boards agreed to seek the state's override-options guidance and campaign-finance rules before any public campaign, and set a joint follow-up for February 9th

why_it_matters: If the boards move forward, residents would eventually vote on an override, which raises the property tax bill outside the normal levy limit -- and the town's April 10th ballot deadline is setting the pace of these discussions.

The named cost drivers -- health insurance, the county retirement assessment, transportation, and a fourth fire shift -- were described as largely fixed, meaning any budget relief this year would have to come from elsewhere or from new revenue.

The unresolved dispute over whether school staffing has grown or been cut touches what positions and services the school budget can protect, and residents will be asked to weigh that when an override figure is presented.
